intro: Hi! You already know can. In this lesson you'll meet its partner, could: to say what you could or couldn't do in the past (When I was five, I could swim), to ask for help more politely (Could you help me?) and to ask for permission (Could I sit here?). Very useful when you travel! Warm-up: could you ride a bicycle when you were six?
teachingNotes: Could is a helper word like can: the same for every subject, followed by the base form (no to, no -s, no -ed). Stress the node's common errors: *'When I was five, I can swim' → 'When I was five, I could swim', *'Could you to help me?' → 'Could you help me?', *'I couldn't went to the party' → 'I couldn't go to the party'. Also expect *'I couldn't walked' and *'I didn't could' → could already carries the past, so the verb after it stays in the base form, and there is no do/did with could.

Name the Indonesian trap: Indonesian 'bisa' never changes ('dulu saya bisa berenang', 'sekarang saya bisa berenang'); the past is shown only with words like dulu, waktu kecil, kemarin. English changes the word itself: can (now) → could (past). Pronunciation: the l in could is silent ('kud'), like would in 'would like'; couldn't sounds like 'kud-nt'.

Could has two jobs in this lesson and they must not be confused. (1) Past ability: there is a past time in the sentence or context (when I was a child, yesterday, last year). (2) Requests and permission (Could you …? / Could I …?) are about NOW: here could is not past, it just makes the question softer and more polite than can, like adding 'kira-kira' in Indonesian. Always say this when a learner asks why 'Could I sit here?' is not past.

Answers: to 'Could you …?' say Sure / Of course / Sorry, I can't (+ a reason) — not 'Sorry, I couldn't'. To 'Could I …?' say Yes, of course / Sure, go ahead / Yes, you can / Sorry, you can't (+ reason). We don't give permission with could ('Yes, you could' sounds like a suggestion), and the answer uses you, not I.

Limits: keep positive 'could' for general past ability (When I was young, I could …). Don't teach 'was able to' / 'managed to' for one successful moment, 'could have', 'Would you …?', 'May I …?' or could for possibility (It could rain). Negative couldn't for one occasion is fine (I couldn't find the hotel). The past simple in this lesson is regular -ed only (walked, called, stayed) plus was/were; avoid irregular past forms (went, had, got, took) except to say 'couldn't went' is wrong.
Context focus is travel: hotels, airports, trains, taxis/ojek, homestays, asking strangers. Keep sentences short and natural.

keyPoints.title: could / couldn't for past ability
keyPoints.explanation: Could is the past of can. Subject + could / couldn't + base verb, the same for every subject: When I was five, I could swim. The verb after could never changes: couldn't go (not couldn't went), couldn't open (not couldn't opened). Questions: Could + subject + verb? Short answers: Yes, I could. / No, I couldn't.

examples.en: When I was five, I could swim.
examples.id: Waktu umur lima tahun, saya sudah bisa berenang.

examples.en: We couldn't find a taxi, so we walked to the hotel.
examples.id: Kami tidak bisa menemukan taksi, jadi kami jalan kaki ke hotel.

examples.en: Could you read when you were four? — No, I couldn't.
examples.id: Kamu sudah bisa membaca waktu umur empat tahun? — Tidak, belum bisa.

id.title: could / couldn't untuk kemampuan di masa lalu
id.explanation: Could adalah bentuk lampau dari can. Subjek (siapa yang melakukan) + could / couldn't + kata kerja bentuk dasar, sama untuk semua subjek: When I was five, I could swim. Kata kerja sesudah could tidak pernah berubah: couldn't go (bukan couldn't went), couldn't open (bukan couldn't opened). Pertanyaan: Could + subjek + kata kerja? Jawaban singkat: Yes, I could. / No, I couldn't.

keyPoints.title: Polite requests with Could you …?
keyPoints.explanation: Could you + verb (+ please)? asks someone to do something for you. It is about now, not the past: could just makes it softer and more polite than Can you …? Good with strangers, hotel staff and your boss. Answer: Sure. / Of course. / Sorry, I can't.

examples.en: Could you help me with my suitcase, please?
examples.id: Bisa tolong bantu saya dengan koper saya?

examples.en: Could you call a doctor, please? — Of course.

id.title: Meminta tolong dengan sopan: Could you …?
id.explanation: Could you + kata kerja (+ please)? dipakai untuk meminta orang melakukan sesuatu untukmu. Ini tentang sekarang, bukan masa lalu: could hanya membuatnya lebih lembut dan lebih sopan daripada Can you …? Cocok untuk orang yang tidak dikenal, petugas hotel dan atasanmu. Jawab: Sure. / Of course. / Sorry, I can't.

keyPoints.title: Permission with Could I …?
keyPoints.explanation: Could I + verb? asks for permission, politely. It is about now, not the past. Say yes with Yes, of course. / Sure, go ahead. / Yes, you can. Say no with Sorry, you can't (+ a reason). Don't answer 'Yes, you could'.

examples.en: Could I open the window? — Sure, go ahead.
Could I park here? — Sorry, you can't. It's for guests only.
examples.id: Boleh saya parkir di sini? — Maaf, tidak boleh. Ini khusus untuk tamu.

id.title: Meminta izin dengan Could I …?
id.explanation: Could I + kata kerja? dipakai untuk meminta izin dengan sopan. Ini tentang sekarang, bukan masa lalu. Beri izin dengan Yes, of course. / Sure, go ahead. / Yes, you can. Tolak dengan Sorry, you can't (+ alasan). Jangan jawab 'Yes, you could'.

could not
couldnt

assessment.prompt: You are at a hotel reception in Yogyakarta. Ask the receptionist politely to call a taxi for you. Start with 'Could you'.
acceptableAnswers: could you call a taxi for me please

assessment.rubric: Correct: Could you call a taxi (for me), please? Without please = 90. 'Could you to call' = 50. 'Can you call a taxi?' = 60 (correct but less polite; the task asks for Could you). 'Could I call a taxi?' = 30 (that asks permission for yourself).

acceptableAnswers: could you show me the way to the station
could you show me the way to the station please
could you please show me the way to the station
assessment.rubric: Correct: Could you show me the way to the station? No 'to' after could. 'Could you showed me' = 50. 'Do you could show me' = 30.

assessment.prompt: You are on a train. The seat next to a woman is empty. Ask her politely for permission to sit there. Start with 'Could I'.

could i sit here please

excuse me could i sit here

excuse me could i sit next to you

may
assessment.rubric: Correct: can (Sure, you can.). 'may' is also correct (more formal). 'could' = 30: we don't give permission with could. 'Sure, I can' = 20 (the answer uses you). 'do' = 0.

blocks.text:
You know **can** (*bisa*) for now: *I can swim.* For the past, English uses **could**: *When I was five, I **could** swim.* The negative is **couldn't** (= could not): *I **couldn't** swim.*
Like can, could is a **helper word** (a small word that stands in front of another verb). It is the same for every subject (*I could, she could, they could*), and the verb after it is in the **base form** (the dictionary form: no -s, no -ed, no to).

id.text:
Kamu sudah tahu **can** (*bisa*) untuk sekarang: *I can swim.* Untuk masa lalu, bahasa Inggris memakai **could**: *When I was five, I **could** swim.* Bentuk negatifnya **couldn't** (= could not): *I **couldn't** swim.*
Seperti can, could adalah **kata bantu** (kata kecil yang berdiri di depan kata kerja lain). Bentuknya sama untuk semua subjek (*I could, she could, they could*), dan kata kerja sesudahnya memakai **bentuk dasar** (bentuk seperti di kamus: tanpa -s, tanpa -ed, tanpa to).

rows.en: When I was five, I could swim.
rows.id: Waktu umur lima tahun, saya sudah bisa berenang.

rows.en: My grandmother couldn't read, but she could cook very well.
rows.id: Nenek saya tidak bisa membaca, tapi dia bisa masak dengan sangat enak.

rows.en: Ten years ago, I couldn't speak English.
rows.id: Sepuluh tahun lalu, saya tidak bisa berbahasa Inggris.
rows.note: *ago* = yang lalu (ten years ago = sepuluh tahun yang lalu).

id.note: *ago* = yang lalu (ten years ago = sepuluh tahun yang lalu).

rows.en: When we were children, we could play in the street.
rows.id: Waktu kami kecil, kami bisa main di jalan.

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap:** in Indonesian, *bisa* never changes. *Dulu saya bisa berenang* and *sekarang saya bisa berenang* both use *bisa*; only *dulu* shows the past. In English the word itself changes: **can** for now, **could** for the past. So *When I was five, I can swim* is wrong: say **I could swim**.
**How to say it:** the **l** in could is silent, like in *would*: could sounds like **'kud'**, and couldn't like **'kud-nt'**.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** dalam bahasa Indonesia, *bisa* tidak pernah berubah. *Dulu saya bisa berenang* dan *sekarang saya bisa berenang* sama-sama memakai *bisa*; hanya kata *dulu* yang menunjukkan masa lalu. Dalam bahasa Inggris, katanya sendiri yang berubah: **can** untuk sekarang, **could** untuk masa lalu. Jadi *When I was five, I can swim* salah: katakan **I could swim**.
**Cara mengucapkannya:** huruf **l** pada could tidak dibaca, sama seperti pada *would*: could dibaca **'kud'**, dan couldn't dibaca **'kud-nt'**.

blocks.prompt: When I was a teenager, I ___ play the guitar.
blocks.explain: 'When I was a teenager' is the past, so use could (not can). The verb comes straight after it, with no to: could play.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: When I was a teenager, I ___ play the guitar.
id.explain: 'When I was a teenager' (waktu saya remaja) adalah masa lalu, jadi pakai could (bukan can). Kata kerjanya langsung sesudahnya, tanpa to: could play.

blocks.text:
**Couldn't** is very useful for problems on a trip: *I **couldn't open** the door, so I called reception.* *We **couldn't find** a taxi, so we walked.*
The verb after could/couldn't **always stays in the base form**. Could already shows the past, so you don't show it a second time: **couldn't open** (not *couldn't opened*), **couldn't go** (not *couldn't went*; *went* is the past of go, but it never comes after could).
Questions: **Could** + subject + verb? *Could you swim when you were five?* Short answers: **Yes, I could. / No, I couldn't.** There is no do/did: not *didn't could*, not *Did you could …?*

id.text:
**Couldn't** sangat berguna untuk menceritakan masalah dalam perjalanan: *I **couldn't open** the door, so I called reception.* (Saya tidak bisa membuka pintunya, jadi saya menelepon resepsionis.) *We **couldn't find** a taxi, so we walked.*
Kata kerja sesudah could/couldn't **selalu tetap bentuk dasar**. Could sudah menunjukkan masa lalu, jadi masa lalunya tidak ditunjukkan dua kali: **couldn't open** (bukan *couldn't opened*), **couldn't go** (bukan *couldn't went*; *went* memang bentuk lampau dari go, tapi tidak pernah dipakai sesudah could).
Pertanyaan: **Could** + subjek + kata kerja? *Could you swim when you were five?* Jawaban singkat: **Yes, I could. / No, I couldn't.** Tidak ada do/did: bukan *didn't could*, bukan *Did you could …?*

rows.en: I couldn't open the door, so I called reception.
rows.id: Saya tidak bisa membuka pintunya, jadi saya menelepon resepsionis.

rows.en: We couldn't find a taxi, so we walked to the hotel.
rows.id: Kami tidak bisa menemukan taksi, jadi kami jalan kaki ke hotel.

rows.en: Rina was sick, so she couldn't go to the party.
rows.id: Rina sakit, jadi dia tidak bisa pergi ke pesta.

rows.en: Could your father drive when he was young? — Yes, he could.
rows.id: Apakah ayahmu sudah bisa menyetir waktu masih muda? — Ya, bisa.

blocks.text: **Could for one moment:** use **couldn't** freely for one problem at one time (*I couldn't find my ticket yesterday*). For a general skill in the past, use **could** or **couldn't** (*When I was ten, I could ride a bicycle*). For one success at one moment, English usually uses other words, which come later; for now, use **could** for things you were able to do in general.

id.text: **Could untuk satu kejadian:** **couldn't** bebas dipakai untuk satu masalah pada satu waktu (*I couldn't find my ticket yesterday*). Untuk kemampuan umum di masa lalu, pakai **could** atau **couldn't** (*When I was ten, I could ride a bicycle*). Untuk satu keberhasilan pada satu saat tertentu, bahasa Inggris biasanya memakai kata lain, yang akan dipelajari nanti; untuk sekarang, pakai **could** untuk hal yang dulu memang bisa kamu lakukan secara umum.

options: I didn't could finish my work.
blocks.explain: After could/couldn't the verb stays in the base form (finish, not finished), because could already shows the past. And there is no did with could.

id.explain: Sesudah could/couldn't, kata kerjanya tetap bentuk dasar (finish, bukan finished), karena could sudah menunjukkan masa lalu. Dan tidak ada did kalau memakai could.

blocks.text:
You know **Can you help me?** for asking someone to do something. **Could you help me?** means the same, but it is **more polite**. Use it with strangers, hotel and airport staff, your boss, or anyone you want to be extra polite to.
Pattern: **Could you** + base verb … (**please**)? *Could you help me with my suitcase, please?*
**Wait, isn't could the past?** Not here. *Could you help me?* is about **now**. In English, a past-looking word makes a question softer and less direct, so it sounds more polite. It's like adding *kira-kira* in Indonesian: *Kira-kira bisa tolong bantu saya?* How to tell the two jobs apart: past ability has a past time (*Could you swim **when you were five**?*); a request asks for help now (*Could you open the door?*).

id.text:
Kamu sudah tahu **Can you help me?** untuk meminta orang melakukan sesuatu. **Could you help me?** artinya sama, tapi **lebih sopan**. Pakai untuk orang yang tidak kamu kenal, petugas hotel dan bandara, atasanmu, atau siapa saja yang ingin kamu hormati.
Pola: **Could you** + kata kerja dasar … (**please**)? *Could you help me with my suitcase, please?*
**Tunggu, bukankah could itu masa lalu?** Di sini bukan. *Could you help me?* tentang **sekarang**. Dalam bahasa Inggris, kata yang bentuknya seperti masa lalu membuat pertanyaan lebih lembut dan tidak terlalu langsung, jadi terdengar lebih sopan. Mirip menambahkan *kira-kira* dalam bahasa Indonesia: *Kira-kira bisa tolong bantu saya?* Cara membedakan dua tugas ini: kemampuan masa lalu punya keterangan waktu lampau (*Could you swim **when you were five**?*); permintaan tolong meminta bantuan sekarang (*Could you open the door?*).

rows.en: Could you help me with my suitcase, please?
rows.id: Bisa tolong bantu saya dengan koper saya?

rows.en: Could you write the address for me, please?
rows.id: Bisa tolong tuliskan alamatnya untuk saya?

rows.en: Could you say that again, please?
rows.note: Very useful when you don't understand.

id.note: Sangat berguna kalau kamu tidak mengerti.

rows.en: Could you call a doctor, please? — Of course.

blocks.text:
**How to answer:** yes = **Sure. / Of course. / No problem.** No = **Sorry, I can't** + a reason (*Sorry, I can't. I'm very busy.*). Answer with **can't**, not *couldn't*: the request is about now.
**No to:** *Could you help me?*, not *Could you to help me?* (like *bisa tolong bantu*, nothing in between).

id.text:
**Cara menjawab:** ya = **Sure. / Of course. / No problem.** Tidak = **Sorry, I can't** + alasan (*Sorry, I can't. I'm very busy.*). Jawab dengan **can't**, bukan *couldn't*: permintaannya tentang sekarang.
**Tanpa to:** *Could you help me?*, bukan *Could you to help me?* (seperti *bisa tolong bantu*, tidak ada kata di tengah).

blocks.prompt: You are in a taxi and it's very hot. You want the driver to turn on the AC. What do you say?
options: Could you to turn on the AC, please?
Could I turn on the AC, please?
Could you turn on the AC, please?
blocks.explain: You want the driver to do something, so use Could you + base verb, with no to. 'Could I …?' asks permission to do it yourself.

id.prompt: Kamu di taksi dan udaranya sangat panas. Kamu ingin sopirnya menyalakan AC. Apa yang kamu katakan?
id.explain: Kamu ingin sopir melakukan sesuatu, jadi pakai Could you + kata kerja dasar, tanpa to. 'Could I …?' meminta izin untuk melakukannya sendiri.

id.title: Meminta tolong dengan sopan: Could you …?

blocks.text:
You know **Can I come in?** for permission (*boleh saya …?*). **Could I …?** is the polite version: *Could I open the window?* *Could I pay by card?*
Again, this is about **now**, not the past: *Could I sit here?* = *Boleh saya duduk di sini?* (now). Could only makes it more polite.
**Answers:** yes = **Yes, of course. / Sure. / Sure, go ahead.** (*go ahead* = silakan) or **Yes, you can.** No = **Sorry, you can't** + a reason, or **Sorry, …** + a reason (*Sorry, this seat is taken.*).

id.text:
Kamu sudah tahu **Can I come in?** untuk meminta izin (*boleh saya …?*). **Could I …?** adalah versi yang lebih sopan: *Could I open the window?* *Could I pay by card?*
Sekali lagi, ini tentang **sekarang**, bukan masa lalu: *Could I sit here?* = *Boleh saya duduk di sini?* (sekarang). Could hanya membuatnya lebih sopan.
**Jawaban:** ya = **Yes, of course. / Sure. / Sure, go ahead.** (*go ahead* = silakan) atau **Yes, you can.** Tidak = **Sorry, you can't** + alasan, atau **Sorry, …** + alasan (*Sorry, this seat is taken.* = Maaf, kursi ini sudah ada orangnya.).

rows.en: Could I open the window? — Sure, go ahead.
Could I pay by card? — Yes, of course.
rows.id: Boleh saya bayar pakai kartu? — Ya, tentu.

rows.en: Could I park here? — Sorry, you can't. It's for guests only.
rows.id: Boleh saya parkir di sini? — Maaf, tidak boleh. Ini khusus untuk tamu.

rows.en: Could I check in early? — Sorry, the room isn't ready.
rows.id: Boleh saya check-in lebih awal? — Maaf, kamarnya belum siap.

blocks.text:
**Answer with can, not could:** *Could I park here? — Yes, you **can**.* We use could to **ask** politely, but not to give permission: *Yes, you could* sounds like a suggestion, not a yes.
**Answer with you, not I:** the other person asked about themselves, so *Yes, **you** can* (not *Yes, I can*). In Indonesian *boleh* is enough, but English needs **you**.

id.text:
**Jawab dengan can, bukan could:** *Could I park here? — Yes, you **can**.* Could dipakai untuk **meminta** dengan sopan, tapi tidak untuk memberi izin: *Yes, you could* terdengar seperti saran, bukan jawaban 'boleh'.
**Jawab dengan you, bukan I:** orang itu bertanya tentang dirinya sendiri, jadi *Yes, **you** can* (bukan *Yes, I can*). Dalam bahasa Indonesia cukup *boleh*, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **you**.

blocks.prompt: A guest asks you: 'Could I use the Wi-Fi?' You say yes. Choose the best answer.
blocks.explain: To give permission, say Yes, of course / Sure / Yes, you can. 'Yes, I could' talks about you (and we don't answer with could), and 'No, I couldn't' is a no about the past.

id.prompt: Seorang tamu bertanya kepadamu: 'Could I use the Wi-Fi?' Kamu mengizinkan. Pilih jawaban terbaik.
id.explain: Untuk memberi izin, katakan Yes, of course / Sure / Yes, you can. 'Yes, I could' membicarakan dirimu sendiri (dan izin tidak dijawab dengan could), dan 'No, I couldn't' adalah penolakan tentang masa lalu.

assessment.cc-5: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Could you to show me the way to the station?
assessment.cc-6: Kamu di kereta. Kursi di sebelah seorang perempuan kosong. Minta izin kepadanya dengan sopan untuk duduk di situ dalam bahasa Inggris. Mulai dengan 'Could I'.
assessment.cc-7: Seorang turis bertanya kepadamu: 'Could I take a photo of your shop?' Kamu mengizinkan. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: Sure, you ___.
